message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Properties**

| Category | Property | Typical Value / Description |
|----------|----------|-----------------------------|
| **Basic Identity** | Symbol | H |
| | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Isotopes | ¹H (protium), ²H (deuterium), ³H (tritium) |
| **Physical State at STP** | Phase | Gas |
| | Boiling point | –252.9 °C (20.4 K) |
| | Melting point | –259.2 °C (14.0 K) |
| | Density (gas, 0 °C, 1 atm) | 0.0899 g L⁻¹ |
| | Molar volume (ideal gas) | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| | Specific heat (gas, 25 °C) | 28.8 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Heat of vaporization | 0.449 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Heat of fusion | 0.0005 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Enthalpy of formation (gas) | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ (by definition) |
| | Standard entropy | 130.68 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Dipole moment | 0 (non‑polar) |
| | Ionization energy | 13.598 eV |
| | Electron affinity | 0.754 eV |
| | Polarizability | 0.666 Å³ |
| | Refractive index (visible) | ~1.000132 |
| | Speed of sound (in H₂ gas) | ~1270 m s⁻¹ (at 20 °C) |
| **Chemical Properties** | Oxidation state | +1 (in most compounds) |
| | Common compounds | H₂O, H₂O₂, H₂SO₄, HCl, NH₃, CH₄, etc. |
| | Acidic behavior | Acts as a weak acid (hydrogen ion donor) in aqueous solution |
| | Basic behavior | Forms hydrides (e.g., LiH, CaH₂) with metals |
| | Redox behavior | Strong reducing agent (e.g., in metal hydride formation) |
| | Combustion reaction | 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O (exothermic, ΔH ≈ –286 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | Bond dissociation energy (H–H) | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Bond length (H–H) | 0.74 Å |
| | Spectral lines | Lyman, Balmer, Paschen series (UV/visible/IR) |
| **Isotopic Variants** | Protium (¹H) | Stable, most abundant (~99.98 %) |
| | Deuterium (²H) | Stable, ~0.02 % natural abundance |
| | Tritium (³H) | Radioactive (half‑life 12.32 y), used in nuclear fusion & radiolabeling |
| | Isotopic effects | Deuterium forms stronger bonds (e.g., D–D > H–H), affecting reaction rates and vibrational spectra |
| **Applications & Significance** | Energy carrier | Hydrogen fuel cells, rocket propellant |
| | Industrial uses | Ammonia synthesis (Haber process), methanol production, petroleum refining |
| | Biological role | Essential component of water, organic molecules, and metabolic pathways |
| | Astrophysical relevance | Most abundant element in the universe; key in stellar nucleosynthesis |
| | Environmental impact | Clean combustion (only water vapor), but storage & transport challenges |

---

### Quick Takeaways

- **Lightest element**: Hydrogen is the simplest atom, with one proton and one electron.
- **Highly reactive**: Forms a wide variety of compounds, from simple diatomic gas to complex organics.
- **Energy potential**: As a clean fuel, it offers high energy density per mass (though low per volume).
- **Isotopic diversity**: Deuterium and tritium bring unique nuclear and chemical properties.
- **Fundamental to science**: From quantum mechanics (hydrogen atom as textbook model) to cosmology (hydrogen’s role in the Big Bang).

Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper details on any specific property or application!
